name: The Plane Tree of the Capuchos Convent Yard
species: London Plane (Platanus x hispanica), species per one source

location.address: Convento dos Capuchos, Estrada dos Capuchos / EN 247-3, 2705-177 Colares

access: Paid entry, Parques de Sintra monument (hours and prices: https://www.parquesdesintra.pt/en/plan-your-visit/opening-times-and-prices/). Not read for this tree; check before writing.
transport: Not verified; the convent is on the Sintra to Colares road in the Serra de Sintra, well outside the town centre. Bus or car; the writer must not state a walk time.
verify_notes: ONE SOURCE, FLAGGED. Visit Sintra (Camara Municipal de Sintra tourism site, fetched) lists as 'notable isolated specimens cultivated by Man' the leafy plane tree covering the convent yard, the old ash tree in the entrance patio, and unusually large boxwood along the paths. The same page calls the convent forest, with its old oaks, probably the most important example of Sintra's old-growth mountain woods. Convent built 1560 (Visit Sintra), abandoned by 1834. Page GPS for the convent: 38 47 03.8 N, 9 26 17.3 W = 38.78439, -9.43814; this is the monument point, not the trunk, so approximate with a small named site. CONFLICT: Slow Travel Blog and Portugalwander say the Courtyard of the Crosses (first space a visitor enters, three crosses for Golgotha) is centred on a large tree without naming species; one personal blog says a cork oak. Unresolved whether the Courtyard of the Crosses is the 'convent yard' with the plane tree or the 'entrance patio' with the ash. No girth, height or age found anywhere, so none given; the page should ask the reader. Alive: lifecheck.py RECENT, iNaturalist observation 2026-10-04 within range (https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/407010157), which is not confirmed to be this tree. Species is not seen on any second page. A trunk-level pin would need a visit or a mapped photo. Ground managed by Parques de Sintra, so owner-page corroboration (parquesdesintra.pt Capuchos page) was looked for and not found naming the tree.
